dialogues.speaker: Bulgakov
dialogues.text: Had I known this was going to happen, I'd never have opted to become a rural doctor. All this travel... *Sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Bulgakov
dialogues.text: N—nothing. Oh, you look like one of those noble-minded individuals who are willing to listen to others pour out their troubles...

dialogues.speaker: Bulgakov
dialogues.text: It's just that... I'm feeling a little vexed about my work. It took me so much effort to graduate from medical school with decent results. But now, I have no choice but to travel on these trains day in, day out to treat patients in far-off villages and towns...

dialogues.speaker: Bulgakov
dialogues.text: Not only are the living conditions in these places poor, sometimes, they can't even afford to pay me my fee. *Sigh* But what am I supposed to do, right? When there's a sickly patient lying right there?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why don't you look for another job then?

dialogues.speaker: Bulgakov
dialogues.text: Another job... But all those years I've spent at the Royal Military Academy studying medicine... and all those years of practice... all of that would go to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Bulgakov
dialogues.text: I have my father to think of, too. *Sigh* He's always wanted me to be a doctor. It's a respectable-enough job, and brings in the Mora...

dialogues.speaker: Bulgakov
dialogues.text: Goodbye... *Sigh* What do I do about my future...?
